title: Transportation Alternatives Program
overview: The Transportation Alternatives Program (TAP) is a competitive grant program that uses federal transportation funds designated by Congress for specific activities that enhance the intermodal transportation system and provide safe alternative transportation options. These investments support place-based economic development by offering transportation choices, promoting walkability, and improving quality of life.Applicants must have legal control of the project property for construction and permanent operations and maintenance. Applicants are required to provide documentation of public input, a resolution of support from their legislative body, and must commit to operating and maintaining the constructed facility in perpetuity. Projects that demonstrate a competitive concept, a high likelihood of constructability, and support for local Complete Streets policies are prioritized.Eligible projects include pedestrian and bicycle facilities (such as shared use paths, bike lanes, and safety improvements), Safe Routes to School (SRTS) infrastructure and non-infrastructure programs, and the preservation of historic transportation facilities. All proposed design elements must meet state and federal design standards without exceptions.Applications may be submitted online at any time through the MDOT Grant System (MGS). The application process requires detailed documentation including an engineer's construction cost estimate, plan view drawings, cross-section drawings, and photographs. Applications are reviewed in multiple cycles each year by the Application Review Committee (ARC). Show More
